- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true outcomes often spike higher, particularly after a dip or low point.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts tend to overshoot and then gradually decline — suggesting a lag in adjusting to new market conditions.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — true prices often revert to higher levels after a dip, while model holds onto the low.
- Forecasts are too smooth and lack volatility — true outcomes show more pronounced swings, especially in the last 10–15 days.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-period spikes — particularly in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts appear to be anchored to recent low values, failing to anticipate sudden upward momentum from market events.
